2_8_cav_song_re_valley_attachment.location: Song Re Valley / Nuoc Dinh Valley, southern Quang Ngai Province
2_8_cav_song_re_valley_attachment.note: 2/8 Cav (organically 1st Brigade) air-assaulted into the area north of the Song Re Valley on 3 Aug, then into LZs in the Song Re Valley itself (north of 5/7 Cav) on 9 Aug, operating alongside 5/7 Cav (organic 3rd Brigade) and 2/12 Cav under what the document titles a '3d Bde reconnaissance in force.' This is the THIRD 1967 instance found of 2/8 Cav operating outside its organic 1st Brigade chain (after the Feb-Apr Pershing OPCON to 3rd Brigade in AD0385642, and the unresolved question of its brigade assignment in AD0386215/May-Jul). Not formally labeled 'OPCON' in this passage the way the Bolling attachment below is, but the operational grouping under 3rd Brigade's recon is unambiguous from the narrative.

2_8_cav_OPCON_to_173rd_abn_bde.location: west of Tuy Hoa, Phu Yen Province
2_8_cav_OPCON_to_173rd_abn_bde.note: Explicitly stated: '1 ACD released TF 2/8 Cav OPCON to 173d Abn Bde effective 17 Sep 67. 2/8 Cav air assaulted into LZ's in the BOLLING AO on 19 Sep 67. 2/8 Cav operations terminated on 14 October when they returned to the PERSHING AO.' The General Situation paragraph independently confirms: 'The 2/8 Cav conducted operations for four weeks under the control of the 173rd Abn Bde in Operation BOLLING.' This is the clearest, most explicitly labeled OPCON statement found for 2/8 Cav in any of the three 1967 documents reviewed.

3rd_brigade_OPCON_to_americal.location: I Corps Tactical Zone (Chu Lai / Tam Ky vicinity, then Hill 63/LZ Baldy)
3rd_brigade_OPCON_to_americal.note: 3rd Brigade (3 battalions plus support elements -- 1/7, 2/7, 5/7 Cav) was placed OPCON to the Americal Division effective 1 Oct 67, deploying over 100km to I CTZ; continuing beyond the end of this reporting period. This is the second consecutive quarter 3rd Brigade has been sent outside the division's own AO under someone else's OPCON (after GREELEY/4th Inf Div in AD0386215) -- a genuinely recurring pattern for this brigade in 1967, not a one-off.

a_1_69_armor_released_to_4th_id.note: Company A, 1/69 Armor (4th Infantry Division), which had been OPCON to the 1st Cav Division for Pershing since at least March 1967 (see AD0385642, AD0386215), had its OPCON released back to the 4th Infantry Division effective 25 Sep 67 -- ending a roughly 6-month cross-attachment.

1_50_inf_mech_attached.note: 1/50 Infantry (Mechanized) Battalion arrived at Qui Nhon from CONUS and was newly attached to the division, becoming operational in the CRESCENT area on 29 Sep 67 -- a new unit, not a reassignment of an existing 1st Cav battalion.

2_7_cav_OPCON_to_IFFV_unchanged.note: Task Force 2/7 Cav continued OPCON to I Field Force Vietnam for Operation BYRD throughout this quarter, unchanged from the prior two 1967 documents.

operations.name: PERSHING
operations.controlling_unit: 2-3 brigades (varying from 3 brigades/7 battalions to 2 brigades/4 battalions over the quarter)
operations.note: Continuing in northeastern Binh Dinh Province; cumulative enemy losses as of 31 Oct: 1134 KIA, 194 POW, 31 returnees. A distinct sub-operation, the 3rd Brigade reconnaissance-in-force into the Song Re Valley (1-19 Aug 67, southern Quang Ngai), is recorded separately below since it involved 2/8 Cav directly.

operations.name: PERSHING sub-op: 3d Bde reconnaissance in force, Song Re Valley
operations.note: 5/7 Cav air-assaulted into Nuoc Dinh Valley 1 Aug; 2/12 Cav into Song Re Valley 2 Aug; 2/8 Cav into the area north of Song Re Valley 3 Aug. 5/7 Cav shifted into Song Re Valley (west) 6 Aug. On 9 Aug, 2/8 Cav air-assaulted LZs in Song Re Valley north of 5/7 Cav -- A/2/8 Cav came under heavy automatic weapons/mortar/57mm RR fire from an estimated 2-3 NVA companies in fortified positions immediately on landing (see events). 2/12 Cav air-assaulted further north on 13 Aug. Redeployment to the Pershing AO began 18 Aug, final elements closed 20 Aug. Results: 42 enemy KIA, 2 POW, 242 detainees; friendly 7 KIA, 44 WIA (whole 3-Bn force).

operations.name: JOIN HANDS
operations.controlling_unit: 3 US battalions (1/5 Cav, 1/8 Cav, 2/12 Cav, 2nd Brigade) + 2 ARVN battalions (Marine TF Bravo, 22d Inf Div)
operations.note: Joint US/ARVN operation, amphibious + air-assault landings around the Cay Giep mountains; no major enemy force encountered, sporadic contacts only. Results: 10 enemy KIA, 5 POW; friendly 0 KIA, 12 WIA (1st Cav Div); ARVN 11 KIA/13 WIA/1 POW/8 detainees separately tallied.

operations.name: BOLLING
operations.controlling_unit: 173rd Airborne Brigade (2 battalions) + TF 2/8 Cav (OPCON'd, see task_organization)
operations.note: IFFV-directed operation west of Tuy Hoa; 2/8 Cav released OPCON to 173rd Abn Bde 17 Sep, air-assaulted into the AO 19 Sep, operations terminated 14 Oct with return to the Pershing AO. Results: 21 enemy KIA, 12 POW, 8 small-arms captured; friendly 0 KIA, 7 WIA.

operations.name: WALLOWA
operations.controlling_unit: 3rd Brigade (1/7, 2/7, 5/7 Cav + support), OPCON to Americal Division
operations.note: Rapid deployment (advance party 30 Sep, brigade CP + 2/12 Cav closed Chu Lai 1 Oct evening, full brigade closed by 2 Oct, air assaults began 3 Oct) into I Corps Tactical Zone in response to a deteriorating situation requiring III MAF reinforcement. Repelled two major enemy attacks (one on a Bn CP/firebase, one on a helicopter landing area) and made one major contact with elements of 3 NVA battalions, plus daily small contacts. Results as of 31 Oct: 675 enemy KIA, 17 POW; friendly 46 KIA, 480 WIA -- by far the highest-casualty operation of the quarter for the division, though it does not involve 2/8 Cav (which was still finishing Bolling with the 173rd through 14 Oct, separately from 3rd Brigade's own move).

operations.name: DAZZLEM
operations.note: Camp Radcliff/TAOR base security. Named significant actions this quarter: a command-detonated mine ambush of a 24-vehicle convoy on Hwy 19 (2 Sep, 6 US KIA, 20 US WIA, 17 vehicles damaged, not attributed to a battalion); an enemy mortar attack on the Hwy 19 firebase (3 Sep, 1 US KIA, 11 US WIA); a combat action of 5/7 Cav along Hwy 19 (17 Sep, 6 US KIA including the unit's CO/XO/FO/Asst FO, 7 US WIA -- notable in that 5/7 Cav is organically 3rd Brigade, appearing here in a Dazzlem-TAOR action rather than with its own brigade); and an attack on a Pacific Architects & Engineers site (3 Oct, 1 US KIA, 1 Korean civilian KIA). Cumulative enemy losses as of 31 Oct: 20 KIA, 1 POW, 25 detainees.

operations.name: BYRD
operations.controlling_unit: Task Force 2/7 Cav, OPCON to I Field Force Vietnam
operations.note: Continuing in Binh Thuan Province, unchanged in structure from the two prior 1967 documents. Cumulative results as of 30 Oct: 734 enemy KIA (a large jump from the 190 reported as of 31 Jul), 94 POW, 1131 detainees; friendly figures given separately by RF/PF vs. 1st Cav elements.

operations.name: VOTER / VOTER II
operations.controlling_unit: division-wide, in conjunction with 23d Inf Div (ARVN) and civilian police
operations.note: Election-security operations for two separate elections in Binh Dinh Province; division deliberately minimized its visible presence near polling sites while providing an outer security ring. No casualty figures given -- an administrative/security posture, not a combat operation.

events.location: Song Re Valley, north of 5/7 Cav's positions
events.notes: The single clearest 2/8-Cav-specific combat citation found in the entire 1967 backfill: A/2/8 Cav received heavy automatic weapons, mortar, and 57mm recoilless-rifle fire from an estimated 2-3 NVA companies in fortified/camouflaged positions immediately upon air assault landing. Company pulled back, 46 sorties of TAC Air conducted, 12 enemy automatic-weapons positions engaged from the air; a second company reinforced in the afternoon but contact could not be regained. Battlefield search found 8 NVA KIA, 5 small arms, 2 crew-served weapons; division estimated 20-30 additional enemy KIA. Not the D Company platoon, and not tied to any KIA in the current roster -- but the clearest confirmation that 2/8 Cav sub-units were in direct, heavy contact during this quarter.

events.location: Nui Mieu cave complex, vic CR 015771
events.notes: 13-day siege of a suspected 50-100 NVA cave complex; the division's most successful single operation of the quarter (only 1 US WIA against 33 NVA KIA + 41 NVAC/detainees).

Night probe/attack by an estimated 2 VC platoons against D/1/8 Cav's defensive perimeter; two VC squads eliminated while attempting infiltration. Not 2/8 Cav -- flagged only because 'D/1/8' is easily confused with 'D/2/8' (D Company, 2/8 Cav, our unit of interest) at a glance; this is 1/8 Cav's D Company, a different battalion entirely.
Two-stage mortar/RR attack; a preplanned 'Mad Minute' security measure is credited with disrupting what was assessed as a larger coordinated attack.

B/1/9 Cav located a suspected 95th VC Bn / 2d VC Regt HQ site via Kit Carson Scout; 2nd Brigade air-assaulted 1/5 Cav (-) in on 30 Aug. Captured 2 Chicom radios of a type found only at regimental level.
Extended probing/mortar/small-arms action over roughly 8 hours by an estimated reinforced enemy company; 9 friendly WIA (figure partially illegible in OCR). No US KIA stated for this specific action.
events.confidence: medium (OCR noise on exact friendly casualty figures)

events.notes: Command-detonated mine ambush of a 24-vehicle convoy travelling Pleiku to Qui Nhon; estimated 200-man enemy force engaged from a 700m killing zone. A/1/7 Cav gun jeeps responded but could not establish contact. 17 vehicles damaged.
Mortar attack (~60 rounds 60mm/82mm) on a Hwy 19 firebase.

A Rome-plow team was hit by a B-40 rocket; escalated into a day-long fight involving ARA, a UH-1 shot up on the highway (pilot killed), TAC Air, and an RF company. IPW readout indicated 5/7 Cav's prompt action disrupted a planned 30-vehicle ambush; the intercepted enemy FO reported his own company CO/XO/FO/Asst FO killed. Notable for naming 5/7 Cav (organically 3rd Brigade) operating on a Dazzlem/Hwy-19 TAOR mission rather than with its own brigade.
ARVN (40th Regt) sighted a VC company; 1st Brigade scouts engaged first, then B/1/8 Cav moved in with 6 tanks and 3 D-7 bulldozers for systematic search and destroy; 46 bunkers destroyed.
A squad guarding a bridge with an M42 Duster was attacked by an estimated 15-25 man enemy force using grenades, M-79s, AK-47s, and B-40 rockets. Bridge undamaged.

events.location: An Lao Valley, vic BS 777114 and vic BS 754196
events.notes: Two separate small contacts/document finds (typewriter and 22nd NVA Regt documents at one site; an arms cache including 82mm mortars and 75mm RRs at the other), aided by a Hoi Chanh guide. This is the exact date-range of santoroski-michael's death (DOD 1967-09-26, though his wounding was 6 Sep by land mine, unrelated to this action) -- flagged for proximity only; this document does not narrate the mine incident that actually wounded him.
events.confidence: medium (unit not specified beyond 'a company' / 'another Co')

events.notes: ~15 VC infiltrated a compound through cut wire, threw an estimated 200 satchel charges; 3 VC killed inside the compound. 1 Korean civilian and 1 Vietnamese civilian also killed/wounded.
Multi-day search and destroy; C/1/9 Cav made initial contact 10 Oct, D/1/5 Cav air-assaulted in and made further contact 11 Oct. 8 NVA Hoi Chanhs picked up from the same area five days later.

events.location: W Cay Giep Mtns, vic BR 9287
events.notes: Night attack on a company perimeter using rocket launchers and small arms; the newly-arrived 1/50 Inf (Mech)'s first named contact in this document.

cross_ref_flags: santoroski-michael's DOD (1967-09-26) falls exactly on the date of event 12 (An Lao Valley small contacts), but that action is unrelated to his actual land-mine wounding on 6 Sep 67 (per the existing event page santoroski-mine-1967-09-06) -- flagged so the 26 Sep date coincidence is not mistaken for a second incident.

This document does not narrate the 6 Sep 67 land-mine incident that wounded santoroski-michael at all, despite covering the full 1-31 Aug/1-30 Sep/1-31 Oct window -- consistent with the pattern (confirmed across all three 1967 documents) that division-level ORLLs only narrate actions the division itself judged 'significant,' and individual mine-strike casualties routinely fall below that threshold even when fatal.
